{{nihongo|'''Kurumano Shrine'''|久留真神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ise Province]].

'''Kuruma Shrine''' (くるまじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine located in Shiroko, [[Suzuka City]], [[Mie Prefecture]]. It is listed in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]] and its former shrine rank was {{ill|UNKNOWN|qid=Q90139226|lt=Ken-sha1=Ken-sha}}. It is also commonly known as '''Fukutoku no Miya''' (ふくとくのみや) and '''Kuruma no Megami''' (くるまのめがみ)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prefectural Shrine Office Kuruma Shrine|url=https://jinja-net.jp/jinja-all/jsearch3all.php?jinjya=2997|access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>.

== History ==  
The date of its original founding is unknown. In ancient times, it is said that [[Ōkuninushi|Ōnamuchi no Mikoto]] and [[Suseri-Hime|Suserihime no Mikoto]] were enshrined in what was commonly called Ise no Mori (the present-day Shiroko area). During the reign of [[Emperor Yūryaku]], Ayanorihime no Mikoto was additionally enshrined and revered as a goddess of good fortune<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mie Prefecture Shrine Office Kuruma Shrine|url=http://kyoka.mie-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/%e4%b9%85%e7%95%99%e7%9c%9f%e7%a5%9e%e7%a4%be/|access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>. During the reign of [[Emperor Bidatsu]], it was divided and enshrined at {{ill|Ise-Kuruma Shrine|ja|伊勢久留麻神社|qid=Q128866991|lt=Ise-Kuruma Shrine}} in [[Awaji Province]]<ref>{{Cite web|title=Awajishima Tourism Association|url=https://www.awajishima-kanko.jp/manual/detail.html?bid=374|access-date=2025-12-31}}</ref>. In Kan'ei 11 (1634), it was relocated to its present location. In April 1943 (Shōwa 18), it was promoted from {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}} to Prefectural shrine<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mie Prefecture Shrine Office Kuruma Shrine|url=http://kyoka.mie-jinjacho.or.jp/shrine/%e4%b9%85%e7%95%99%e7%9c%9f%e7%a5%9e%e7%a4%be/|access-date=2025-12-4}}</ref>.

== Enshrined Deities ==  
* Main deity: Ōnamuchi no Mikoto
* Associated deities: Suserihime no Mikoto, Ayanorihime no Mikoto<ref>{{Cite web|title=Prefectural Shrine Office Kuruma Shrine|url=https://jinja-net.jp/jinja-all/jsearch3all.php?jinjya=2997|access-date=2025-12-30}}</ref>

== Annual Festivals ==  
* Second Saturday and Sunday of April
* Hatsuuma Festival: First Sunday of March
* Tenno Festival: Second Sunday of July
* Rituals are listed in [https://dl.ndl.go.jp/pid/1257927/1/54 Special Rituals in Mie Prefecture]
